Subject: SIG Questionnaire initiation — next steps & clarifying questions

Jordan — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Demo recap: Redwood hosted inference, dedicated/private deployment options, and audit trail capabilities. You asked specifically about SOC 2, HIPAA posture, and encryption options.
- Next step: we'll kick off the SIG questionnaire so your security team has our standard form to review. I attached the initial SIG (sig-questionnaire.xlsx) — most customers treat this as an "initiation" that we complete collaboratively.

A few clarifying questions your security team usually asks, so if you can flag these internally it will speed the response:
1) SOC 2: Do you need a current SOC 2 Type II report, or is an attestation of SOC 2 in-progress acceptable initially?
2) PHI/HIPAA: Will Aurora be sending PHI to Redwood (i.e., do we need a BAA)?
3) Data residency: any requirements to store or process data in a specific US region/state?
4) Encryption & key mgmt: do you require customer-managed keys (CMK) or is provider-managed encryption acceptable?
5) Questionnaire owner & timeline: who on your side will own the SIG and what timeline are you targeting for completion?

Attachments: sig-questionnaire.xlsx (stub)
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example_shared_security_docs (Redwood security packet)

Cc'ing Marissa from our security team to help with technical clarifications. Happy to hop on a quick follow-up call with your security lead — tell me a few windows that work and we'll book.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes

Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SIG Questionnaire initiation — next steps & clarifying questions

Hi Camila — thanks for the follow-up and the questionnaire. We appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from our side and a partial upload of our responses attached.

- SOC 2: We are currently working toward SOC 2 Type II; expected completion by 2026-08-20. For procurement, an attestation that SOC 2 is in-progress is acceptable for now, but we will need the final report when available.
- HIPAA/PHI: Aurora is a covered provider for certain business lines — we'll likely need a BAA. For the initial integration we anticipate sending pseudonymized data only, but please assume PHI could be in scope.
- Data residency: All production PHI must remain in US regions; we prefer us-east-1 but can accept us-west if that simplifies deployment.
- CMK: Our security team prefers customer-managed keys for any PHI workloads, but not mandatory for non-PHI test data.

Attached is a partially completed copy of the SIG with our security team's notes (aurora_sig_partial.xlsx). I'll loop in our security mailbox (security@aurorahealth.com) who will take lead on completing the rest. They may have additional clarifying questions around key rotation, KMS provider, and logging/retention windows.

We'll aim to have the full questionnaire back in ~10 business days, but can accelerate if we schedule a short working session.

Best,
Jordan
Director, Product Integrations
Aurora Health

Thanks Jordan — that timing makes sense. A few follow-ups / clarifications from Marissa and me that will help your security team complete the SIG: 

1) SOC 2 exchange: once Aurora has the final SOC 2 Type II, we can provide a secure download link (PDF) under an NDA or via our portal — let us know the preferred method.
2) BAA: Redwood supports BAAs; our legal can start that discussion. For engineering, please confirm if there are any required clauses beyond standard Redwood BAA (we can share a template).
3) Encryption: Redwood supports AES-256 at rest and TLS1.2+ in transit. For CMK scenarios we integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault) — can you confirm which KMS you plan to use? Also let us know if you require envelope encryption.
4) Key rotation & retention: our default is 90-day rotation for service-managed keys; when using CMKs your org controls rotation policy. Logs are retained per the account plan — we can provide a retention table in the shared Drive.
5) Audit logs & access: we can provide token-level access logs and per-route tracing; if your team wants a sample log extract format, Marissa can attach one.

Proposed next step: Marissa (cc'ed) and I can run a 30-minute working session with your security lead to walk through the SIG and the CMK options. Suggested times: Thu 16 Jul 09:00–11:00 PT or Fri 17 Jul 13:00–16:00 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks — we'll also upload the Redwood security packet with the encryption/KMS extracts into the Drive link I sent earlier.

Camila Reyes
